Merging of the Cantonese rising tones

Source: R/data.R
cantonese_tone_merger.Rd

Hong Kong Cantonese has two rising tones, T2 (high rising, 25) and T5 (low rising, 23), which some younger speakers merge. 90 speakers aged 18 to 75 each produce 10 T2 and 10 T5 words; the size of the f0 rise is measured in semitones. For a sound change in apparent time and for individual differences: mergers form a separate group of speakers, most of them young.

Usage

cantonese_tone_merger

Format

A tibble with 1800 rows and 7 columns:

speaker

S01 to S90.

age

Age in years.

gender

"female" or "male".

word

w01 to w20.

tone

"T2" or "T5".

log_freq

log10 word frequency, 1 to 5; no effect.

rise

f0 rise from onset to offset in semitones.

Source

data-raw/cantonese_tone_merger.R

Details

True model: each speaker is a merger with probability 0.65 * plogis((40 - age) / 6). Non-mergers rise by 7 semitones in T2 and 3.5 in T5; mergers by 5.6 and 4.8. By-speaker intercepts have SD 0.6 and token SD is 0.9. The design follows reports of T2/T5 merging (Mok, Zuo & Wong 2013); the data are simulated.

References

Mok, P. P. K., Zuo, D. & Wong, P. W. Y. (2013). Production and perception of a sound change in progress: Tone merging in Hong Kong Cantonese. Language Variation and Change, 25(3), 341-370. doi:10.1017/S0954394513000161

Examples

head(cantonese_tone_merger)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   speaker   age gender word  tone  log_freq  rise
#>   <fct>   <int> <fct>  <fct> <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 S01        42 male   w01   T2        3.14  8.24
#> 2 S01        42 male   w02   T2        3.65  8.65
#> 3 S01        42 male   w03   T2        3.67  9.24
#> 4 S01        42 male   w04   T2        2.88  7.58
#> 5 S01        42 male   w05   T2        2.39  7.11
#> 6 S01        42 male   w06   T2        3.18  7.54
